# 60-second usability check: Results page

WS-RESULTS-SIMPLE. Source: office hours with Greg Miller, 2026-11-09, action item 7 ("can they explain the
result back within 60 seconds?"). Ben runs this on one person who has not seen Lotline. Record the result below;
append a new run for each version of the page, never edit an old one.

## Setup

- **Who:** one adult who has not seen the project and does not work in housing or modeling.
- **What they see:** the published app (`challenge.toml` → app URL), Results section, North Carolina, ADUs,
  on a laptop screen. Do not scroll for them and do not explain anything.
- **Time:** 60 seconds of looking, starting when the page is on screen. Then take the page away.

## Script (read it as written)

> "This page is about a proposed state housing law. Take one minute to look at it. Then I'll take it away
> and ask you three short questions. There are no wrong answers; I'm testing the page, not you."

After 60 seconds, close the page and ask, one at a time:

1. **How many more homes?** "About how many extra homes would this law lead to?"
2. **Compared with what?** "More than what? What is it being compared to?"
3. **How sure are we?** "How sure is the page about that number?"

## Scoring

| Question | Pass looks like | Fail looks like |
|---|---|---|
| 1. How many more | A number near the median, or the range ("a few hundred", "between X and Y") over five years | No number; a baseline number; a yearly number taken as the total |
| 2. Compared with what | "Compared with not passing the law" / "what would get built anyway" | "Compared with now", "with other states", or no answer |
| 3. How sure | Mentions a range, or that it was checked against past years | "Very sure" with no range; or "no idea" |

Pass = all three. Note the exact words they used: wording they reach for is copy we should steal.
